### 1) What is on the screen
The frame is a 100-pixel-tall dusk harbour strip over a solid black void: orange / peach sky at the top [0,0,256,32], medium-blue water with thin horizontal highlights [0,32,256,32], grey brick quay wall with blue mortar [0,64,256,36], then flat black [0,100,256,140] to the bottom of the 256 x 240 frame. The eye goes first to the tiny dark T-shaped mooring-post / lamp silhouette against the peach sky near center-top in region x, y, w, h = 112,16,24,24. I cannot see any player, enemy, HUD, prompt or text, so I cannot see what the player is being asked to do.

### 2) Does it look like a real NES game
(a) palette count reads as NES - PASS: 9 distinct colours, all measured as 64-entry NES palette entries and well under at most 25 colours on screen at once, 58.3% is one backdrop colour which matches NES use of one shared backdrop.
(b) shading is flat, one colour per shape - PASS: sky, water and brick are flat fills, no gradient banding or alpha that would violate no gradients, no alpha.
(c) sprites read at a glance - FAIL: I cannot see any sprites in this frame to judge; a battle frame with no 8 x 8 or 8 x 16 objects in OAM means no silhouette to read.
(d) no anti-aliasing and no soft edges - PASS: all edges I can see are hard 1-pixel steps on the 8 x 8 tiles grid, including window / stripe borders.
(e) colour changes land on 16 x 16 grid - FAIL: the water highlight stripes at [0,36,256,28] change blue-to-light-blue every 2-4 pixels vertically and the brick blue mortar lines at [0,64,256,36] cut inside 16 x 16 pixel boundary blocks, which a background can change palette only on a 16 x 16 pixel boundary - this would need extra 4 background palettes of 4 entries to do on hardware.

Measured numbers do not contradict this: size is 256 x 240 pixels, 9 colours inside ceiling, all NES entries.

### 3) Composition and text
Crowded in the top band [0,0,256,100], completely empty in the bottom [0,100,256,140] which is 58.3% of the frame as solid black. The focal T-post at [112,16,24,24] is at the top edge where the player never looks during a battle; the needed focal area - center / lower third where sprites and damage numbers would live - is empty black. Text regions: I cannot see any text in the full 256 x 240 - no HUD, no dialogue, no score. Worst is the missing HUD row at [8,216,240,16]: illegible because absent, cannot be read at 256 x 240 without guessing.

### 4) What looks AI generated or off
Not AI-diffusion - no pillow shading, no mangled glyphs, no muddy gradients. It looks handmade and honest programmer placeholder, but off as a shipped design: 1) composition reads as prompt instead of design - "quay dusk" strip pasted over empty black, no ground plane for battle; 2) detail without structure in brick at [0,64,256,36] - same grey box repeated with 1-pixel blue mortar that has no doors, edge, coping stones; 3) borders that are not a whole number of tiles - water-to-brick transition around y~64-68 does not snap to 8 pixels, sky stripes look like fill-tool bands; 4) large empty field of single backdrop colour with zero tile variation; 5) tiny centered dark object with 1-pixel legs that has no clear 8 x 8 silhouette and no shadow / base.

### 5) Five concrete fixes
1. Region [0,104,256,136]: fill black $0F void with 16x16 ground tiles using BG palette 0: $0F Black backdrop + $00 Dark Grey + $10 Light Grey + $30 White, add 8-pixel-high HUD bar at bottom, do not leave 140px of shared backdrop.
2. Region [0,32,256,32]: snap waterline to y=32 and make water bands 8 pixels tall minimum, move current 2-pixel highlight rows down by 8 pixels to y=40 and y=48 so every colour change starts on an 8-pixel tile row and 16-pixel attribute row.
3. Region [0,64,256,36]: simplify brick to one 16x16 BG palette - replace blue mortar $12 Medium Blue with $00 Dark Grey, keep $10 Light Grey brick face only, redraw mortar as 1-pixel $0F Black lines on 16-pixel grid so no 16x16 block needs 2 palettes.
4. Region [112,16,24,24]: enlarge T-post silhouette to 16 wide x 32 tall on the 8 x 8 grid, move left by 8 pixels to [104,16,16,32], give it 1-pixel $0F Black outline and fill $00 Dark Grey so it reads as sprite, not stray pixels.
5. Region [16,216,224,16]: redraw one text row on the 8x8 glyph grid - add "HP 28/28" in $30 White on $0F Black, 8x8 pixels per character, no proportional / anti-aliased font.

### 6) Scores and machine readable block
nes_authenticity: 6 - palette-legal but attribute-illegal and unfinished.
readability: 3 - no sprites, no text, focal point in wrong place, bottom half void.
charm: 4 - honest dusk bands have some appeal but no character.
